executiveSummary: GM0766 passes the deterministic execution contract for all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, 27,495 residents, seventeen neighbourhoods, two BAG places and three generated NWB links are coherent; exact-zero behavior, determinism, cumulative event-attributable service-pressure person-hours, causal ledgers, reconciliation and layer invariance also pass. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Eight unrelated canonical hazards use exactly the same seventeen-neighbourhood ordering because the allocator does not include hazard type, source containment or a selected hazard surface. This conflicts with the municipality's hydraulic stress test: it identifies named cloudburst streets in West 2, Oud Dongen, Centrum, Biezen and Tichelrijt, and identifies Tichelrijt 1/2 and Wildert as heat-sensitive while rural areas and Klein Dongen are cooler. The model instead ranks Buitengebied Oost first for pluvial and heat, Tichelrijt eleventh and West 2 thirteenth. The major-river preset also turns distance to an approximate national line into 1.641118 internal flood stress, 14,258 affected residents at T+24 and 14,588 at T+72 without selecting a defence failure, probability band, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Official evidence distinguishes no high-probability inundation, at most 1.5 m in named medium/small-probability areas, and an exceptional 1-in-10,000 band up to 5 m north of 's Gravenmoer; those mutually exclusive scenarios cannot be replaced by one municipality scalar. Public data can materially improve context: a daily Brabantse Delta FeatureServer supplies local water-system geometry and the deployed national registers include 59 selected water/wastewater points, 40 antenna sites and 15 education locations. None proves live topology, controls, capacity, backup or restoration. Current observations remain separate from hypothetical T+72 output, and empty provider, care, Waterinfo, air, seismic or road-event queries remain Unknown rather than zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Dongen / Provincie Noord-Brabant / Waterschap Brabantse Delta
evidenceSources.title: Klimaatstresstest Gemeente Dongen
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive report, 12 May 2020; underlying analyses include 2018 imagery and then-current climate scenarios
supports: A local InfoWorks ICM surface model was run for 70 mm in one hour, 90 mm in one hour and 160 mm in two hours, assuming a full sewer and surface routing. It identifies Middellaan, Oude Baan, Monseigneur Nolens- and Schaepmanlaan, Procureurweg, Steenstraat and Kanaalstraat as the most vulnerable roads/building interfaces; Thorbeckelaan, Minister Goselinglaan, Berlagestraat, Molendijk/Kerkebos and nearly all streets in Vaart add named access concerns.

PDOK Locatieserver road centroids place those named streets in West 2, Oud Dongen, Centrum, Biezen, Tichelrijt and Hoge Akker. This geocoding is an audit cross-check, not a replacement for the report's native raster or road geometry.

The report's thermal image identifies Tichelrijt 1/2 and Wildert as heat-sensitive due to hard surface and limited green, with Tichelrijt around 38 degrees Celsius and about 10 degrees warmer than surroundings in the cited 26 July 2018 image. Rural areas, rural cores and Klein Dongen are described as cooler. It identifies drought/low-groundwater vegetation sensitivity north of 's Gravenmoer and east of Dongen and water-quality concern at Beljaart Buiten, the canoe/duck ponds and West II ponds.

For inundation it distinguishes no area with a large probability; medium/small-probability cases reach at most 1.5 m west of Lage Ham and at Tichelrijt south of the Wilhelminakanaal, while an exceptional 1-in-10,000 combined map reaches up to 5 m north of 's Gravenmoer. The report explicitly warns that the displayed source scenarios do not all occur simultaneously.

This is a municipality-wide PDF download and static modeled context, not an observation, warning, forecast or current drainage state. No machine API, fixed refresh cadence or explicit reuse licence for its underlying rasters is published on the landing page. Obtain a municipality/owner-authorized native export with scenario, units, resolution, edition, lineage, licence and NoData before causal ingestion.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023–2027
supports: The profile treats digital disruption of vital infrastructure, extreme weather and nature fire as top-five regional priorities. Extreme weather explicitly includes intense rain, drought, cold/snow/ice, heat, storm/tornado and fog, with possible prolonged road/rail, lifeline and responder impacts.

It distinguishes coastal surge, high-river, polder/dike-break and extreme-weather flooding. It describes defence, tide, river-discharge and storm-barrier dependencies and says a high-water wave can last multiple days; it does not provide a Dongen depth surface or authorize the simulator's scalar.

Vital processes include electricity, gas, drinking water, water quantity management, voice/data, internet, GNSS, 112/C2000, road/rail/water transport and payments. The profile explicitly emphasizes cascades, scarcity and interruption of communications, payments and transport control rather than independent service percentages.

Regional nature-fire context includes forest, heath, peat and dune fire; dry conditions, difficult access, extinguishing-water supply, vulnerable people and prolonged deployment are material. This is qualitative regional planning context, not a local live ignition, fuel surface, resource inventory or T+72 commitment.

The downloadable regional PDF is reviewed at least within the statutory four-year cycle and describes ongoing risk monitoring, but no machine hazard API, fixed operational refresh or explicit standard reuse licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Beheerregister waterlopen en kunstwerken and Watersysteemanalyse Beneden Donge
evidenceSources.edition: Live register inspected 2 September 2026; service metadata states daily revision; Beneden Donge analysis definitive 13 December 2018
supports: The integration-ready ArcGIS FeatureServer supports Query/Extract across the Brabantse Delta management area and states daily revision. The Dutch open-data catalogue https://data.overheid.nl/en/dataset/dce0ec2b-23d5-462e-98ef-9e4570c5c19e declares CC0; retain publisher metadata and retrieval time with every extract.

Exact intersection with the consumed GM0766 polygon returned 15 shut-off devices, 109 bridges, 58 pits, 57 weirs, seven fixed dams, one fish passage, 740 culverts, six siphons, 232 category-A watercourses, 840 category-B watercourses, 33 category-C watercourses, 134 bank protections, two water-storage polygons, two drainage/supply areas and nineteen operational-level areas. It returned no in-boundary pumping-station or sluice feature. Counts are geometry/register context, not proof of absence, completeness or operation.

The deployed national HWH subset contains 59 in-boundary display points: two DAMO sewer pumps and the same 57 IMWA weirs. The direct board service therefore adds material culvert, siphon, watercourse, storage and level-area context, but neither source establishes a connected sewer/drainage graph or current control state.

The definitive Beneden Donge analysis is downloadable at https://simcms.brabantsedelta.nl/_flysystem/media/watersysteemanalyse-beneden-donge.pdf. It documents seven manually operated Donge weirs, a siphon under the Wilhelminakanaal with one of two culverts normally closed to reduce Dongen water nuisance, and downstream dependence on gemaal Keizersveer. It is a 2018 system analysis with no fixed refresh or explicit standard reuse licence, not present operation.

Feature attributes such as geometry, type, nominal level, width, name and maximum pump capacity remain inventory context. They do not prove live connectivity, compatible units, flow direction, blockage, setting, condition, power/backup, service availability or restoration. Missing records and null attributes remain Unknown.

No authorized live feeder, pressure zone, complete sewer/wastewater chain, antenna backhaul/coverage, facility continuity, food/fuel/pharmacy stock, priority-customer, crew, vehicle, pump-control, backup or restoration dataset is loaded or inferred.
Official plans, static models, registers, current observations and deterministic exercises retain distinct evidence classes and clocks.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The shared neighbourhood seed, unselected river screen and absent local scenario surfaces conflict with Dongen's published rain, heat, drought and probability-band geography.
notes: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3981-3995 derives hazardSeed only from city seed, scenario seed and region id; hazard type, source containment, terrain and selected hazard surface are absent. The common canonical scenario seed makes severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share one exact seventeen-neighbourhood order.

That order starts Buitengebied Oost, Biezen, West 1, Buitengebied 's Gravenmoer and Wildert. It places Centrum 9th, Oud Dongen 10th, Tichelrijt 11th, Beljaart 12th, West 2 13th, Dongen-Vaart 14th, Buitengebied West 2 15th, 's Gravenmoer 16th and Hoge Akker 17th.

E03's named 70 mm road hotspots map by official Locatieserver centroids to West 2, Oud Dongen, Centrum, Biezen, Tichelrijt and Hoge Akker. The model-first Buitengebied Oost is not the report's primary urban cloudburst hotspot, while several published hotspots rank 9th–17th.

E03 identifies Tichelrijt 1/2 and Wildert as the strongest heat islands and rural/Klein-Dongen areas as cooler. Heat T+24 instead ranks Buitengebied Oost first, Wildert fifth, Tichelrijt eleventh and Klein Dongen seventh, duplicating flood/cyber/winter order rather than the observed 2018 thermal pattern.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-479 computes river exposure from the municipality reference point to one of three approximate line segments and lines 1244-1249 turn it into city-wide forcing. It selects no Dongen defence, Donge/Wilhelminakanaal system state, probability band, connected grid, arrival or recession.

GM0766 has no municipality-specific unsupported-spatial note in packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:533 onward, so the browser displays precise local ranks and a derived-screening river headline without the audit warning already used for reviewed peers.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipal ledgers close and expose evidence class, dependency order, operational assumptions and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; every service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; weighted service shortfalls sum to municipal pressure.
System-pressure weights are power 0.18, water 0.15, drainage 0.08, gas 0.09, telecom 0.12, mobility 0.12, facilities 0.14 and supply 0.12, totaling one.
Dependency chains, local-context factors, drivers, recovery progress and restore-service counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.

Household preparedness changes modeled people/supply consequences rather than physical fragility. Day type, start clock, demand, backup, network and repair multipliers are normalized and labeled scenario assumptions; interventions are response-delayed and do not masquerade as actual Dongen crews/assets.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure relative to a matched no-event baseline before intermunicipal transfers and apply a preparedness multiplier. They are a modeled burden proxy, not observed outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.

Compound retains flood/cyber forcing and pressure worsens from 0.625888 to 0.638048 by T+72, showing the sustained-forcing guard is active; its local amplitude and consequences remain unsupported.

E03's probability bands and E04's prolonged high-water/cascade mechanisms show that persistence is plausible in some events, while E05–E06 show real controlled-water dependencies. They do not select this event or calibrate the T+72 state.

findings.summary: One hazard-blind seed gives eight unrelated hazards exactly the same seventeen-neighbourhood ordering.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3981-3995 omits hazard type, source containment and selected hazard geometry from hazardSeed. Severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Buitengebied Oost/Biezen/West 1 first through third and Tichelrijt/West 2/Hoge Akker 11th/13th/17th. findings.summary: The cloudburst map contradicts Dongen's named hydraulic road/building hotspots and does not run the published rainfall events.
findings.evidence: E03's InfoWorks ICM analysis uses 70/90 mm in one hour and 160 mm in two hours and identifies hotspot roads in West 2, Oud Dongen, Centrum, Biezen, Tichelrijt, Hoge Akker, 's Gravenmoer and Vaart. No rain cell, terrain, sewer/storage state, catchment, culvert, siphon, pump control or receiving level governs that distribution.

findings.summary: A municipal reference-point distance produces precise sustained water without selecting one of Dongen's mutually distinct flood events.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-479 uses three approximate national line segments and lines 1244-1249 convert proximity into an internal flood-stress amplitude. Dongen receives 1.641118 stress, severity 0.509707, 14,258 affected at T+24 and 14,588 at T+72. E03 distinguishes no high-probability inundation, at most 1.5 m west of Lage Ham/Tichelrijt for medium/small-probability cases and up to 5 m north of 's Gravenmoer only in an exceptional 1-in-10,000 combined map that explicitly does not occur everywhere at once. E05–E06 show real controlled Donge/Wilhelminakanaal and defence dependencies but select no breach, defence state, level, connected footprint, probability, arrival or recession.

findings.summary: The heat/drought map reverses published Dongen thermal context and reuses the flood/cyber neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: E03 identifies Tichelrijt 1/2 and Wildert as heat-sensitive, with the cited Tichelrijt surface around 38 degrees Celsius and roughly 10 degrees warmer than surroundings, while rural areas and Klein Dongen are cooler. It separately identifies low-groundwater vegetation exposure north of 's Gravenmoer/east of Dongen and named pond-quality locations. Canonical heat T+24/T+72 uses 23.961198 degrees Celsius and drought 0.507763, ranks Buitengebied Oost first, Wildert fifth, Klein Dongen seventh and Tichelrijt eleventh, exactly matching seven unrelated hazard maps. The official 2018 thermal image is dated context, not a current observation, but it falsifies the claim that the shared order represents Dongen heat geography.
findings.action: Mark GM0766 local heat/drought ranks unsupported. Seek the municipality/owner-authorized native thermal and drought surfaces with acquisition time, surface-versus-air-temperature semantics, scenario horizon, resolution, licence, cadence and NoData. For live exercises, combine static susceptibility with a valid-time KNMI product and explicitly separate air temperature, surface temperature, drought, water quality and population vulnerability; add a regression that Tichelrijt/Wildert context is not overwritten by rural hash order.

findings.summary: T+72 persistence and service restoration are bounded model assumptions, not a Dongen forecast or resource plan.
findings.evidence: River flood stress/severity remain 1.641118/0.509707 from T+24 through T+72, pressure rises to 0.516587 and cumulative burden to 1,009,804.72; only facilities availability changes, falling from 0.534149 to 0.473339. Compound pressure likewise worsens to 0.638048. E03–E08 provide no selected event recession, local road passability, control state, pump/utility backup, crew/vehicle/material inventory, shelter activation, supply stock or restoration schedule. E04 supports possible multi-day forcing/cascades but not these exact values.
findings.action: Keep the trajectory labeled as an assumption/sensitivity envelope and never imply actual dispatched crews or assets. Once a named hydraulic event is selected, bind repair eligibility to recession/access and expose bounded, editable response delay, backup and repair capacity with provenance. Until authorized resource data exists, retain transparent synthetic priors and Unknown operational state.

findings.summary: Public water objects materially improve context but cannot support exact first-72-hour drainage and drinking-water availability.
findings.evidence: E05's daily FeatureServer intersects 57 weirs, six siphons, 740 culverts, 1,105 classified watercourse features, two storage areas and nineteen level areas, while the deployed national subset displays two sewer pumps and 57 weirs. River T+24/T+72 water and drainage availability 0.521507/0.352164 and compound 0.365161/0.295643 come from generic dependencies rather than catchment/sewer/pipe topology, blockage, receiving level, valve/weir setting, compatible capacity, power/backup, contamination, treatment or operator state. The absence of an in-boundary board pumping-station feature is not proof of no pumping dependency; E05 documents downstream Keizersveer control outside the boundary.
findings.action: Integrate the daily CC0 Brabantse Delta register as versioned display/context alongside weekly CC BY-SA HWH IMWA and variable-contributor DAMO, preserving source type, timestamp, units and no-feature semantics. For causal use seek municipality-authorized GWSW and security-reviewed board/Brabant Water topology/state covering catchments, sewer, culverts/siphons, controls, treatment/receiving water and emergency power. Until then keep named subsystem assumptions and exact service percentages explicitly synthetic.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning-model audit, not validation against an observed Dongen disaster, outage, evacuation, casualty, health, welfare or restoration dataset.

The CBS 2025 generalized boundary supports municipal aggregation but not parcel hydraulics, drainage catchments, defence compartments, asset ownership, utility zones, road approaches or incident perimeters.

Dongen's 2020 climate stress test is strong local modeled evidence but is dated; its native rasters, exact metadata and explicit reuse terms are not exposed through a current machine API. Historical imagery/model output must not be relabeled as current observation.
The 2023–2027 regional risk profile supplies mechanism and cascade context, not local event forcing, live state, probabilities, resource inventories or restoration promises.

The 2018 Beneden Donge analysis documents system structure and then-current controls but cannot establish 2026 configuration or operation. The daily register is current inventory context but not live control telemetry or complete topology.
LIWO products require expert event/version/terms/NoData selection and do not independently provide current defence condition, rainfall, drainage control or recovery resources.

RWS 70 mm/2 h and AHN4 are national modeled-scenario/terrain context and differ from Dongen's local 70/90 mm per hour and 160 mm per two hours events; neither provides current rainfall, sewer state or recession.
Provider/capacity/antenna/school/care/station/GTFS records are partial dated context, not complete connectivity, load, capacity, occupancy, coverage, backup, stock, access or restoration commitment.

No reviewed safe public source supplies complete Enexis, Brabant Water, sewer/treatment, gas, Ziggo/backhaul, facility, food/fuel or emergency-resource topology/state; security-sensitive detail was not inferred.

First-72-hour household behaviour, medical dependence, visitors, responders, mutual aid, shelters, buses, pharmacies, fuel/food stocks, pump controls, crew travel and repair priorities remain scenario assumptions or Unknown.
